data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004 (case-split on zero presence: 144 + 504 = 648) and SRC_005 (direct positional: 9 × 9 × 8 = 648) share mechanism only superficially: SRC_004's case-split is a restricted partition over the value of a single digit (zero), while SRC_005's positional product is invariant over digit identities and counts slots. Their convergence is necessary only because 144 + 504 = 9 × 9 × 8 happens to hold arithmetically; they are not mechanically equivalent. This is refuted if an algebraic identity other than the specific numeric coincidence 144 + 504 = 648 forces the two mechanisms to agree for arbitrary digit alphabet sizes (e.g., if we generalize to base-b, the case-split yields (b-1)(b-1)(b-2) + (b-1)(b-1) ≠ (b-1) × b × (b-1) in general, breaking the identity at non-decimal bases).
